'''Andrei Dmitriyevich Linde''' ({{langx|ru|Андрей Дмитриевич Линде}}) is a Russian-American [[Theoretical physics|theoretical]] [[physicist]] and the [[Harald Trap Friis]] Professor of Physics at [[Stanford University]].

==Inflationary multiverse and eternal chaotic inflation==

Linde and his Stanford colleague Vitaly Vanchurin calculated the number of all possible universes, to be about <math>10^{10^{16}}</math> if we do not consider the fact that humans as observers are limited in their ability to distinguish more universes. If this is taken into account, there could be as many as <math>10^{10^{10^{7}}}</math> universes. By analyzing the [[Inflation (cosmology)#Slow-roll inflation|slow-roll inflation]] mechanism that initially generated the [[quantum fluctuations]], the scientists could estimate the number of resulting universes at <math>10^{10^{10^{7}}}</math>.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://phys.org/news/2009-10-physicists-parallel-universes.html|title = Physicists Calculate Number of Parallel Universes}}</ref>

== Inflation and string theory ==

One of the main challenges of this theory is to find the [[probability]] of living in each of these different parts of the universe. However, once string theory is invoked, it is extremely difficult to return to the previous picture of a single universe. In order to do so, one would need to prove that only one of the many vacua of string theory is actually possible, and to propose an alternative solution of the many problems which can be solved by using the anthropic cosmological principle in the context of the theory of inflationary multiverse.,<ref>{{Cite journal |title=de Sitter Vacua in String Theory |journal=Reports on Progress in Physics |volume=80 |issue=2 |page=022001 |arxiv=1512.01203 |last=Linde |first=Andrei |year=2015 |bibcode=2015arXiv151201203L |doi=10.1088/1361-6633/aa50e4 |pmid=28071600 |s2cid=5221573}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=The Cosmic Landscape: String Theory and the Illusion of Intelligent Design (Publisher: Little, Brown and Company)|url=https://archive.org/details/cosmiclandscapes00suss|url-access=registration|last=Susskind|first=Leonard|year=2005|publisher=Little, Brown and Company |isbn=978-0-316-15579-3}}</ref>

Linde  continues his work on the theory of inflationary multiverse. In particular, [[Renata Kallosh]] and  Andrei Linde, together with their collaborators, developed a theory of cosmological attractors. This is a broad class of versions of [[inflationary cosmology]] which provide one of the best fits to the latest observational data.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Planck 2015 results. XX. Constraints on inflation|journal=Astronomy and Astrophysics|volume=594|issue=A20|pages=A20|arxiv=1502.02114|last1=Ade|first1=P.A.R.|display-authors=et al|year=2016|doi=10.1051/0004-6361/201525898|doi-access=free|bibcode=2016A&A...594A..20P|s2cid=119284788}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==

He was a co-recipient, with Alan Guth and [[Alexei Starobinsky]], of the [[Kavli Prize]] awarded by the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref name="AAAS">{{cite web |title=Nine Scientists Share Three Kavli Prizes |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/nine-scientists-share-three-kavli-prizes}}</ref>

== Personal life ==

Linde is married to [[Renata Kallosh]]. They have two sons.<ref>{{cite web |title=Renata Kallosh |publisher=[[UCLA]] |url=http://cwp.library.ucla.edu/Phase2/Kallosh,_Renata@882345678.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040925072509/http://cwp.library.ucla.edu/Phase2/Kallosh,_Renata@882345678.html |archive-date=September 25, 2004 |access-date=March 17, 2014 }}</ref>

== Political positions ==
In February–March 2022, he signed an open letter by Russian scientists condemning the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://t-invariant.org/2022/02/we-are-against-war/ |title=Открытое письмо российских учёных и научных журналистов против войны с Украиной |date=24 February 2022 |access-date=2 April 2022 |language=ru |trans-title=An open letter from Russian scientists and scientific journalist against the war in Ukraine}}</ref> and another open letter by Breakthrough Prize laureates with the same message.<ref>[https://breakthroughprize.org/News/69 An open letter from Breakthrough Prize laureates]</ref>
